component-metadata.author: knimeuser
component-metadata.description:
Metanode to filter input data frame using selected column values based on the column specified percentile.
Numerical and text (string) columns can be both selected for filtration.
At first, values in the selected column are ranked and rank percentile is computed within the given column. Ranking is from the lowest to highest value (numbers) or alphabetically (text column), i.e. in ascending order and missing values are ignored. The values ranks and percentiles are returned as new columns ("filtering column_rank" and "filtering column_percentile"). 'Ranking method' settings can be used to define how to treat same values groups ranking with these options: - average: average rank of group - min: lowest rank in group - max: highest rank in group - first: ranks assigned in order they appear in the array - dense: like 'min', but rank always increases by 1 between groups.
pandas.DataFrame.rank is used for rank and percentile calculations, see http://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/generated/pandas.DataFrame.rank.html for its full documentation.
Percentile values are used for a rows based filtering of the input table. During the rows filtering step these two metanode settings are considered: - percentile threshold - from 0 to 1; e.g. 0.9 = 90% - operator - e.g. is greater than ('>')
Rows having rank percentile passing the specified threshold and operator (e.g. greater than 0.9) will appear in the top output table, otherwise they will be in the bottom one. Rows with missing value are returned in the bottom output table as well.
Example: goal - to get rows having the 10 % of the highest values in the specified column (i.e. rank percentage should be equal or higher to 0.9) percentile threshold - 0.9 operator - '>=' ranking method - 'average'
